newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Dole fund-raiser sentenced to home confinement.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Dole fund-raiser sentenced to home confinement.

text.p: A former vice chairman of Bob Dole's presidential campaign finance committee on Wednesday was sentenced to a year's probation with six-months of home confinement for "repeatedly and blatantly" violating federal campaign laws.
U.S. District Judge William Young also ordered Simon Fireman, 71, to pay a $1 million fine.
Federal prosecutors had sought a six-month prison term for Fireman, owner of an Avon, Massachusetts-based sporting goods company, which was fined $5 million in a separate action.
Judge Young instead chided federal prosecutors and accused the government of "manipulating its charges in order to suit the (sentencing) guidelines."
The judge also had harsh words for Fireman, who admitted trying to conceal $120,000 in campaign contributions, more than half of it for Dole's presidential bid.

When Fireman's lawyer, Thomas Dwyer, argued his client's behaviour was an aberration, the judge hotly replied: "I reject entirely that this was aberrant conduct. This wasn't aberrant conduct. This was a planned and calculated conspiracy."

"Mr. Fireman, make no doubt about it. This was tainted money to pollute the (political) process," the judge told the tall, gray-haired defendant. "Your sentence should have been more than six months and it should have been spent in prison."

But the judge said prosecutors had tried to design their charges based on stiffer sentencing guidelines that would have called for Fireman, who admitted to funnelling campaign contributions to both Democrats and Republicans, to serve a prison sentence.

"We're pleased that the court accepted our recommendation of home detention," Dwyer told reporters at a hastily called news conference after the sentencing. Fireman, surrounded by family and friends, rushed out of the courthouse and did not attend the news conference.
Dwyer said Fireman would begin his sentence in three weeks at his home in Quincy, Massachusetts.

Prosecutors, who said earlier Fireman hoped to be named an ambassador in a Dole adminstration, were not happy with the reduced sentence. During the three-hour hearing, Assistant U.S. Attorney Joseph Savage argued that home confinement was akin to "sending him to his room."
But later, Savage said in a telephone interview: "We're satisfied justice was served."

Fireman's company, Aqua-Leisure Industries, Inc. was told to pay a $5 million fine and placed on four years probation. The company must pay $1 million within 14 days and the rest in six-month instalments of $500,000 until the full sum is paid.
